title: Heavily skewed tenant: tenant_id = (select setting) hides the value from statistics
issue: The InitPlan parameter's value is unknown at plan time, so tenant_id = $param is estimated as 1/ndistinct and the MCV list (tenant 1 = 50% of rows) is ignored. The (select ...) wrap that fixes per-row evaluation causes this.
symptom: naive_rls: row estimate for the big tenant is ~scale/2000 against ~scale/2 actual (see est/actual q-error in the plan table); the planner picks nested loops / BitmapAnd / index walks sized for a tiny set, and the error compounds through the join (join_devices). Small tenants are fine. best_practice_rls (stable expression, stats-visible) estimates correctly but evaluates the function per row.

scale.meaning: rows in app.events (tenant 1 = 50%, tenant 2 = 10%, tenant 3 = 5%, the other 35% spread over ~2000 tenants); 20000 devices.

subjects.name: small
subjects.note: one of ~2000 tiny tenants (~0.02% of rows)
